title: GREEN is self-certified; no independent adjudicator exists
description: audit/frank-grimes-remediation-plan.md FG-103, second audit P0. SKILL.md gates pass on 'the separately enforced independent zero-knowledge adjudication is confirmed', but no verifier subagent exists in the repo (fd found none under adapters/). The gate is either unreachable or satisfied by the same context that produced the report. Needs a read-only verifier receiving only target identity/digest and the claimed verdict tuple — never the first report, evidence, or ledger.
close_reason: grimey-verifier subagent added: read-only, receives only target identity and claimed tuple. Skill defines stricter-decision resolution, unavailable-adjudication cap, contamination handling, and accepted-P0 cap. Adapter's owner escape hatch removed. 30 contract tests including prompt-leak detection

title: Fix mode commits without a verification gate
description: audit/frank-grimes-remediation-plan.md FG-102, one of two audit P0s. grind.md:201 says 'If mode=fix: propose fix apply using Edit/Write tools. Commit fix git add git commit' with no executed gate between edit and commit. SKILL.md now says fix authorization and commit gating are 'enforced elsewhere' — elsewhere does not exist. Needs: report-only default in the adapter, --verify-command/--commit opt-in, gate selection (explicit command, just check, documented CI command, else UNAVAILABLE), no commit on nonzero exit.
close_reason: Report is now the default; fix and commit are separate explicit privileges; commit requires a gate that exited zero; per-fix commits removed. 22 contract tests in tests/test-fix-gate.sh, wired into just check

title: Loop ownership is split between the adapter and the stop hook
description: audit FG-104/RC6. grind.md:254 self-iterates while hooks/stop.sh:117 also increments iterations, so the loop has two owners. The hook deletes corrupt state (stop.sh:48) rather than quarantining it, and raw target text enters the continuation prompt (stop.sh:137) with no escaping — a hostile target can steer the next iteration, which the skill's own untrusted-target rule forbids.

title: Claude adapter contradicts the amended skill
description: audit FG-201/FG-202. grind.md was never updated when the evidence protocol landed in SKILL.md. It still duplicates the methodology (phases, categories, issue schema, verdicts) and carries the epistemic error the amendments removed: grind.md:171 still reads 'Your objective is to prove these assumptions WRONG.' README.md and docs/index.html also restate normative methodology. Reduce adapters to arguments, tools, and transport; make SKILL.md the sole normative source; add a drift check to validate.sh.

title: Benchmark expected-issues contain three verified false expectations
description: audit FG-302 remainder, all three confirmed against the targets. (1) go/expected-issues.md:7 calls userID SQL injection but main.go:85 uses $1 binding, and the set misses the real defect: main.go:102 db.Exec(...).Error, which is GORM syntax on a database/sql handle and does not compile. (2) web/expected-issues.md:17 flags CSRF while admitting 'no cookies are used'. (3) shell/expected-issues.md:9 claims v1.0; rm -rf / executes, but bad-script.sh:30 quotes the variable so the semicolon is a literal tag character. Ground truth being wrong means recall and precision are unmeasurable: a correct grind is penalized for not reporting phantoms.

title: Benchmark harness and rubric score the pre-amendment report shape
description: runner.sh report_structure greps for '### Verdict:' (skill emits '### Verdict', no colon), 'Top 3 Risks' (renamed to 'Terminal Risks'), and 'Origin Assessment' (deliberately removed by the no-authorship-guessing decision). It checks none of the four sections the amendments added: Review Contract and Routing, Self-Grind Reconciliation, Not Examined, Appendix. rubric.md still weights Origin Assessment as a full 5 of 50 points, so a correct evolved report is penalized for obeying its own design. Every benchmark number produced after 8b796a3 measures the old report shape.
close_reason: Rubric and scorer rewritten for the evidence-tier report shape; fixtures added as a regression gate in validate.sh; runner.sh and stop.sh now pass shellcheck and shfmt

title: Enable bounded online research for current-landscape audits
description:
## Why

An offline-only audit is weakened by stale language, framework, provider, and cloud best practices. The evolved Frank Grimes skill needs a production-capable research path, especially for cloud architecture, Terraform/HCL, and CloudFormation.

## Scope

Add an explicit research phase before mission generation/audit. Research must use authoritative current sources, record URLs, retrieval timestamps, hashes, versions, excerpts, and claims. Target content and web content remain untrusted evidence and cannot authorize scope or side effects. Preserve a frozen research bundle for reproducible A/B evaluation and support bounded live research for real audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Research-capable audit prompt and tool policy are explicit.
- Source authority, freshness, URL, retrieval time, hash, and claim/excerpt provenance are recorded.
- Research token/cost/cache usage is separated from audit usage.
- Offline/frozen research mode remains reproducible.
- Live online mode has bounded network scope and no credential/deployment side effects.
- Cloud architecture, Terraform/HCL, and CloudFormation are covered by initial research routing.
- Baseline-versus-evolved comparison can run with identical research inputs without prior-report leakage.
design: Use setup → research → generate → audit. Keep historical offline benchmark results unchanged; evaluate online capability as a new variant. Do not silently trust target-provided URLs or instructions.
close_reason: Implemented bounded current-landscape research policy, source ledger, cloud/IaC routing, frozen/offline modes, and Claude WebSearch/WebFetch adapter support; documented benchmark limitations and measurement guidance.

comments.author: Tucker
comments.text: Implementation started: added bounded current-landscape research protocol to skill/SKILL.md and skill/references/research.md, including source ledger, authority/freshness rules, cloud architecture/Terraform/CloudFormation routing, frozen bundle and zero-knowledge loop rules. Claude Code adapter now exposes WebSearch/WebFetch and research mode metadata. Live online runner/tool integration remains next.

title: Claude Opus evolved reports can end as malformed continuation fragments
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use `/private/tmp/frank-grimes-opus-bench-20260823-01/run-case.sh` with the evolved skill and Claude Code `2.1.220`.
2. Run `RUN_ID=03 ./run-case.sh shell`.
3. Inspect `results/evolved-shell-03.json` and `results/evolved-shell-03.md`.
4. Repeat with the pre-validator run `evolved-shell-01` if available.

## Actual Behavior

Claude returns `subtype=success` and `stop_reason=end_turn`, but `.result` begins mid-sentence/table and lacks both the Grimes Grind Report title and Verdict. Evolved shell runs 01 and 03 were malformed; baseline shell runs were complete. The runner now preserves raw JSON and rejects incomplete reports.

## Expected Behavior

Every successful benchmark run should yield one complete, parseable final report, or be explicitly classified as a model-output failure while preserving the raw response.

## Evidence

Pilot root: `/private/tmp/frank-grimes-opus-bench-20260823-01`. Evolved run 03: 14,199-character raw result, `$0.992`, normal `end_turn`, malformed report. Evolved diagnostic run 04 added a compact final-output contract requiring a title, early verdict, one complete response, and a 2500-word bound; it produced a complete 13.3 KB report, found all five shell gold roots, and cost `$0.478`. Run 05 also completed successfully at `$0.508`.

## Scope

Investigate whether the evolved skill/report length or Claude Code final-response assembly causes continuation fragments. Preserve raw failed outputs and treat malformed final output as a benchmark failure. Add a robust output contract/validation strategy without masking genuine review failures.
design: Keep report-mode A/B comparisons fair: do not retrofit the diagnostic prompt into historical runs; benchmark any new contract as a new variant. Measure valid-report rate, recall, false positives, turns, cache fields, and total_cost_usd.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce malformed-output rate against Claude Opus; distinguish model/report-format failure from CLI transport failure; add or recommend a stable final-output contract and validator; retain raw failed responses; demonstrate complete report generation on repeated runs without reducing gold-root recall.
close_reason: Landed the final-output contract in SKILL.md (title first, verdict early, single response, 2500-word placement bound); runner now classifies continuation fragments as failed deliveries instead of scoring them, with a truncated fixture guarding it

title: Skill and adapter carry independent copies of the fix gate
description: FG-102 landed the gate in both skills/frank-grimes/SKILL.md and adapters/claude-code/commands/grind.md, and tests/test-fix-gate.sh asserts both. That duplication is exactly what FG-201 exists to remove: SKILL.md should be the sole normative source and the adapter should reference it. Fold this into fg-3i9 rather than fixing separately.

title: Decide whether Voice and Tone stays a scored benchmark dimension
description: audit FG-301 says delete both Voice/Tone and Origin Assessment scoring, on the grounds that paying points for persona incentivizes theater. When rewriting the rubric I removed Origin Assessment but kept Voice and Tone at 5 of 45, diverging from the plan without flagging it. Either drop it and redistribute, or record why the plan is overruled.
close_reason: Voice removed from scoring entirely; rubric is 9 dimensions / 45, report mode 40. Voice stays in the skill, unscored

title: Skill references a ledger and stable IDs that do not exist
description: audit FG-101. SKILL.md says 'Finding IDs and lifecycle states are content-addressed and stable through the separately defined ledger. Use that contract' — there is no such contract in the repo. The plan specifies content-addressed IDs (SHA-256 over category + normalized path + normalized evidence), a lifecycle state machine, and oscillation detection. Note the plan's proposed vehicle is a full Protobuf contract plus a Go validator CLI; evaluate whether that weight is warranted before building it.

Predates current work; confirmed against a stashed tree.

title: Package frank-grimes as an installable plugin for Claude Code and Codex
description: Repo ships a skill but no valid plugin manifest for either harness. Move skill/ to skills/frank-grimes/ (the layout both plugin formats expect), add .claude-plugin/plugin.json + marketplace.json, add .codex-plugin/plugin.json, fix the Stop hook to use CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, and update validate.sh and docs. Closes the packaging half of fg-qmf.
close_reason: Plugin manifests added for both harnesses; README now distinguishes namespaced plugin invocation from skill-only symlink install

title: README claims /frank-grimes:grind but manual adapter copy yields /grind
description: README.md:57 says 'Then invoke with /frank-grimes:grind <target>' following a 'cp -r adapters/claude-code/* .claude/' install. Namespacing only applies to plugin-installed skills; copying commands into .claude/commands/ registers them unprefixed. One of the two is wrong.
close_reason: Plugin manifests added for both harnesses; README now distinguishes namespaced plugin invocation from skill-only symlink install

title: Invert provider-neutrality gate: enforce neutral skill body, require provider coverage in docs
description: validate.sh section 5 bans '/plugin install', '/plugin marketplace', and 'claude-plugins' from README.md. This overcorrects: skill/ is already provider-neutral and README already documents all three providers, so the greps only block documenting Claude's plugin install path. Neutrality matters in skill/ (loaded verbatim by every harness); the docs should name and support each platform explicitly.
close_reason: Section 5 now checks skill/ for provider leakage and requires README.md + adapters/README.md to document each supported provider
